intro: You are the catalyst of a young planet. You build nothing: you watch
how the planet lives and step in now and then.
The planet runs on its own. When something important happens (a species
appears, a species dies out, a drought begins), the game stops and asks
what you do. You can also do nothing: the planet will cope in its own way.
Planet values are in everyday units (temperature in °C, rainfall in mm).
One tick is one simulation step, a year has 360 ticks. Lost species
hardly ever return on their own.
The goal? Understand the planet. Keep asking: what happens if...?
quiet: The planet is coping on its own. You can wait (0) or try something new.

heat.text: {species} died out from the heat. Cooling will help, but too much can trigger an ice age.

cold.text: {species} died out from the cold. A light warming may help them return.

drought.text: {species} died out for lack of water. Aquifers raise the humidity of the air; cloud seeding brings rain (good for shrubs and trees, bad for moss and algae).

co2_starvation.text: {species} died out because CO₂ ran short. Volcanoes will supply it, but also warm the planet for a long time.

oxygen_lack.text: {species} died out because oxygen ran short. Algae and plants make oxygen: wait until there is more, and only then sow them again.

poor_soil.text: {species} died out because there was too little soil. Soil comes from the biomass of lower plants: give them time.

fire.text: {species} burned in wildfires. Fires grow with plenty of oxygen and dry air; moisture puts them out.

shade.text: {species} died out in the shade of taller plants. Thinning shrubs or trees will let the light back in.

oxygen_excess.text: {species} retreat as oxygen builds up. That is the natural course of things: they will survive in oxygen-free niches.

old_age.text: {species} were dying faster than they renewed: conditions are at the edge of what they can bear.

culled.text: {species} died out after your thinning. If you want them back, sow them.

hunger.text: {species} died out: nothing left to eat. Let their food plants grow back before they return.

grazed.text: {species} were eaten faster than they grew back. Animals that graze them will thin out on their own.

drought.text: Drought weakens plants and feeds wildfires. Aquifers helped in most droughts; cloud seeding dries the air in a drought.

guardian_healing.text: The Guardian planet heals its own wounds: life regrows faster. Often it is best to wait.

ice_age.text: Ice age: cold slows plants and the ice reinforces itself. A light warming helped in most ice ages; a strong one often did harm.

fire_season.text: Fire season: mostly trees burn and shrubs take their place. No action clearly helped: often it is best to wait it out. Thinning shrubs tends to hurt.

overheating.text: Overheating: the heat slows growth and drains life. Light cooling and aquifers helped; strong dust and volcanoes did harm.

succession.ready: {species}: conditions are good, they will appear on their own or you can sow them.
succession.lost_ready: {species} died out, but conditions are good again: sowing may bring them back.
